1.9 Rust bounded scanner

dng-subset LEFT RIGHT REPORT [--rate-mib N] [--max-new N]
           [--import-cache FILE] [--after SUMMARY]

The binary is rust-scanner/target/release/dng-subset. It has one process and checks one pair at a time using 1 MiB buffers. It recognizes classic TIFF and BigTIFF headers, traverses implemented IFD/subIFD paths and confirms equal selected raw blocks plus their encoding tags. It uses direct byte comparisons, not stored DNG digests. The parser has finite limits for IFD counts, tag counts, selected tag sizes and integer arrays. Unsupported or damaged structures remain unverified unless its exact whole-file fallback proves that the bytes are preserved.

The default --rate-mib 32 accounts for combined raw-data reads in MiB/s; choose any finite number above zero through 512. It is an average pacing budget, not a kernel I/O ceiling for all metadata, filesystem and decoder traffic. --max-new N limits newly checked left files, leaving others pending. Matching names and relative-path priority follow the same basic one-way model as Python.

Unlike Python, Rust does not decode different compression/layouts or compare auxiliary previews and metadata. not-confirmed.tsv reports MISSING, UNVERIFIED and PENDING. A differing encoded block is unverified, not a proven sample difference. Exit 0 confirms complete raw subsumption; exit 1 leaves coverage unconfirmed; parsing/argument/I/O failures are nonzero as well. Always inspect summary.json, which retains total_left, verified_equal, missing_name, unverified, complete and left_subsumed_by_right.

verified.tsv is append-only. Its four columns are hex-encoded left path, hex-encoded right path and comma-separated stamps for both files. Each stamp has device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. Resume retains path membership and checks inode, size, mtime and ctime, deliberately ignoring device number across external volume remounts. It does not hash accepted payloads again. There is no cache version/executable hash bound to this TSV format and no automatic report lock; keep the producing source version and one exclusive owner yourself. A new report directory gives a fresh scan.

--import-cache trusts already verified records in the same format after current identity checks. It is not a way to admit arbitrary filename matches. The export_verified.py helper exports eligible Python raw-equal cache results for explicit roots. Keep its input report and tool provenance.

--after SUMMARY waits until the named file contains the literal "complete": true and both input directories exist, checking once per minute. It does not parse and require a successful subsumption verdict. A completed prior scan can have missing or unverified files. Use this only as a scheduling aid, not a safety dependency, and do not share report directories across jobs.
